title: Best Tools to Test Automation Workflows Before Production
summary: Test automation workflows before production on isolated data copies with the right tools. Find which support rollbacks and promotions for your setup.
body_markdown:
## 1.[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/)


Activepieces gives you run history and unlimited flows on every plan, including free. Releases and Git Sync sit on the Ultimate plan, so on the lower tiers the separation between copy and live is yours to build.


### Confirmed workflow testing features in Make.com


Here's what is confirmed. You can test a single step with sample data before the whole flow runs, so a bad field mapping shows up on one step instead of in your customers' inboxes.


Flows have a draft version that is separate from the published one, so you can edit without changing what is running.


At 2am, run history is how you find out which step broke, because it shows what each execution did. And it's open source, so you can self-host it on a server you control.


### Missing staging environment for Make.com workflows


Without one, "test" means a second flow, or a second self-hosted instance, that you build and keep in sync.


That's the manual step the last section warned about, and no feature removes it for you.


Activepieces fits a team that wants a free, self-hostable visual builder: the core is MIT-licensed, the free plan allows unlimited flows, and there are 750 integrations to build with.


It also needs someone willing to own the discipline: separate test credentials, a written list of what changes on promotion, and a habit of checking run history after every release.


If you're short on budget and long on patience, that trade is reasonable. If nobody will own it, it isn't.


### Community and support


Because separation is something you'll mostly work out from forum answers and shared examples, community size matters here. GitHub's chart compares GitHub stars for Activepieces (25,683), n8n and Temporal.


**Activepieces, at 25,683 stars, sits far below n8n** , an open-source visual workflow builder, and close to Temporal, a code-first workflow engine. Expect fewer ready-made answers than n8n offers.


Next, the platforms that build the separation in, or sell it on a higher plan.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams that treat automation flows as reviewable work, judged on whether a change can be checked before it reaches production.


Its draft version stays separate from the published one, single steps can be tested with sample data, and environments allow promotion from test to production.


Git Sync and Release Management put flows into a review process rather than leaving them only in a vendor's UI, though they sit on the Ultimate plan, so on lower tiers that separation is yours to build.
